diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The agent produced correct Excel structure but used the wrong formula for the gold valuation exposure / RaR. Expected RaR values are ~1.732x smaller than produced (ratio 7.10/4.11 ≈ 1.728 ≈ √3), indicating the agent incorrectly multiplied by √3 in the shock formula. The expected formula is reserves × Z × σ_3m / 100 (without the √3 horizon scaling), but the agent used reserves × Z × σ_3m × √3 / 100. The xlsx skill does not contain task-specific guidance for this RaR calculation methodology, so it needs clarification on the correct 95% one-sided shock formula for this task context.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill provides general spreadsheet construction guidance but offers no domain-specific guidance for financial risk calculations like Reserves-at-Risk (RaR) or 95% one-sided valuation shock. The agent applied an extra √3 horizon scaling factor to the shock formula, producing values exactly √3 times too large. The skill should include a note (or the task-specific calculation conventions) that for a single-period 95% one-sided shock using an already-period-matched volatility (3-month σ), the formula is simply reserves × 1.645 × σ_3m / 100 — do NOT further multiply by √(horizon) because the σ is already at that horizon. Also clarify that RaR% = exposure / total_reserves × 100 using the un-scaled exposure.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a 'Financial risk calculations' subsection under 'Financial models' in xlsx/SKILL.md that specifies: (1) When computing a Value-at-Risk / valuation shock using a volatility that is already measured over the risk horizon (e.g., a 3-month standard deviation), the shock formula is Exposure = Value × Z × σ / 100 (with σ expressed in percent). Do NOT additionally multiply by √(horizon periods) — that scaling is only used to convert a shorter-period σ up to a longer horizon. (2) For a 95% one-sided confidence level, use Z = 1.645. (3) RaR as a percentage of total reserves = Exposure / Total Reserves × 100. Include a brief worked example so the agent does not double-count horizon scaling when the input volatility is already horizon-matched.
